_why: The power metric's tuning surface. Which feats and subsystem features contribute to a character's measured offense and defense, and by how much -- kept in data so the metric is tuned here rather than in power_metric.py. Follows the build_archetypes.json precedent: tune the JSON, not the engine. Every `model` names arithmetic the scorer implements; every `feats` key must match data/feats.csv exactly, which gates/validate_power_metric.py asserts. A curated name that matches nothing is this stack's most repeated bug (orphaned conditionals, the case-mismatch spell drop, 27 silently-unpickable shifter aspects), and here it would silently contribute zero forever.

_assumptions._why: A DPR number is meaningless without the round it describes. These are the conditions the metric assumes; an adder whose `condition` is not satisfied here contributes nothing. Changing an assumption re-scores every character, so they live in data and the baseline report prints them.
_assumptions.round: full attack, single target, round 2 (no charge, no nova, no pre-cast buffs)
_assumptions.nova_round: burst_raw/burst_expected: the fully-juiced fight round (the sweaty pass, ruling 2026-08-11) -- the better of the full-attack routine and the vital-strike standard-action alpha, with limited-use class offense active (rage, smite, challenge, bard song, ki), COMBAT-tier spell buffs pre-cast with no action-economy cap (a declared upper bound), an activated haste item, the best readied strike's dice landing once, size steps applied to the weapon dice, and flanking granted so precision lands
_assumptions.sustained_round_buffs: PERSISTENT-tier buffs (10+ min/level) count in the sustained round too -- they are up before every fight; spheres talent changes and stance dice likewise (martial focus and the stance are always on)
_assumptions.target_ac: the cr_benchmarks.json `ac` for the character's CR (level - 1)

feats._why: Keyed by the exact data/feats.csv `name`. `model` selects the arithmetic; `condition` gates it against _assumptions and the character's actual weapon.

Power Attack.note: -1 attack and +2 damage per 4 BAB; +50% damage if two-handed. Held in code because the two-handed multiplier depends on the weapon, not on a constant.

Deadly Aim.note: The ranged analogue; same -1/+2 per 4 BAB, no two-handed multiplier.

Point-Blank Shot.note: Also +1 damage; inactive under the default assumption set.

Two-Weapon Fighting.note: Inactive by default -- the metric does not model a two-weapon routine (see _blind).

Toughness.note: +3 hp, or +1 per HD at 4 HD and above.

Snapping Turtle Style.note: +2 shield bonus to AC with one hand free -- folded into ac_combat as an upper bound (the free-hand condition is not checked). flat_ac rows land in ac_combat ONLY, never the parity-locked base ac.

Crane Style.note: Amount 0 on purpose: Crane's +1 applies only while fighting defensively and is folded by the POSTURE model (which also halves FD's attack penalty when this feat is held). The row exists so the spine feat resolves against the corpus.

posture._why: The defensive posture (wall pass, ruling 2026-08-12, RAW numbers by ruling -- Pascal's sheet carries house kickers these deliberately skip). Folded into ac_combat and cmd for EVERY character that qualifies: fighting defensively is universal, Combat Expertise is house-ambient (Int 13). The declared trade -- the posture's attack penalties are NOT applied to the offense axes, because ac_combat and dpr describe different rounds (a wall fights defensively; a striker full-attacks).

ac_class._why: Class AC the ledger never carries (the dr-table pattern). Monk AC fires only UNARMORED (armor_ac and shield_ac both 0 -- armor_type_mapping gives monks None, so generated monks qualify).

monk_ac.note: Wis modifier + level/4, unarmored and unencumbered.

stance_ac._why: Curated AC values for PoW stances whose prose does not parse flat ('+N bonus to AC' parses for only 4 of the AC-granting stances; 24 more mention AC with scaled or conditional wording -- a standing curation backlog, add rows as they are verified against Martial_Disciplines.json). Names are the SPACED spellings the payload uses; the validator resolves them against the data file.

Silver Crane Waltz.note: +2, +1 per 8 HD -- verified against Pascal's sheet and the discipline text.

Snapping Turtle Stance.note: +2 shield bonus with one hand free; upper bound, free hand unchecked.

wild_shape._why: The wildshaped wall (defense side only, ruling 2026-08-12). Hours/level duration = persistent: natural armor folds into ac_combat, the Str shift into melee attack/damage in both rounds. Natural-attack ROUTINES stay on the blind list -- the wildshape mauler is a later slice. Bands are typical beast-shape packages by druid level.

rules._why: Structural rules, not name lists. Path of War ships 1,033 maneuvers across 59 disciplines (473 Strikes) and Spheres ships hundreds of talents -- neither carries a structured damage field, only prose. Authoring one entry per maneuver is not a measurement job, so the reducible slice is expressed as rules keyed on what the payload actually exposes.

spheres_destructive_blast.note: The base destructive blast: 1d6 per 2 caster levels, minimum 1d6, as a ranged touch attack. One rule replaces every blast-shaping talent; the talents that change damage TYPE or add riders are declared blind.

pow_readied_strike.note: Deliberately conservative. The overwhelmingly common strike text adds the initiation modifier to the attack's damage, so that is all this models. Per-strike scaling dice and riders vary far too much to curve-fit and are declared blind rather than guessed at. Strike type and level ARE parseable from each maneuver's `Discipline` string (only 12 of 1,033 fail), so a later slice can refine this without new data.

nova._why: The nova round's limited-use class offense (burst_raw axis, ruling 2026-08-11). Keyed by model, then by EXACT class_data.json class name -- chained and unchained variants are separate keys there and separate rows here. Only always-available-when-it-matters abilities: things a character switches on for the fight it cares about. Per-strike PoW dice, kinetic blast and spell damage stay in _blind.

rage.note: Str-equivalent bonus while raging: attack +B/2, damage +B/2 (x1.5 two-handed), melee only. Unchained rage's flat +2/+3/+4 attack-and-damage is modelled with the chained scale -- a slight overstatement for two-handers, accepted and stated. Skald rows are inspired rage granted to self.

smite.note: +Cha to hit and +class level damage on every attack against the smitten target; the benchmark target is assumed smiteable in the nova round.

challenge.note: +class level damage against the challenged target.

sneak_attack.note: dice = (level - start) // per + 1, at d6 -- rogue (L+1)/2, slayer L/3, investigator's studied strike. Gated on nova_flanking; precision dice never multiply on a crit and the scorer honours that. The investigator row is studied strike, close enough to author here rather than model separately.

inspire_courage.note: Competence bonus to attack and damage from the bard's own song. The skald's song is its rage row above, never both.

ki_extra_attack.note: One ki point buys one extra full-BAB attack on a full attack. Stacks with a haste effect (different source); the scorer adds both.

spell_buffs._why: The sweaty-round buff fold (ruling 2026-08-11): every buff the character can CAST counts -- persistent tier (10+ min/level, up before every fight) in BOTH rounds, combat tier (min/level or rounds/level) in the nova round, no action-economy cap, a declared upper bound. Castability = list membership only; the casting-stat minimum (Wis 14 to cast 4th-level buffs) is NOT checked -- another stated upper-bound edge, though the striker stat priority keeps `primary` second precisely so built war-priests stay legal. Effects are MODELED here rather than read from spells/spell_changes.json: that file's formulas are sheet-variable-bound and it covers barely half this list. Every key must match a data/spells.csv name (case-insensitive) -- gates/validate_power_metric.py asserts it, the silent-nothing rule. Caster level = capped character level, the blast rule's own upper bound. Offensive effects fold into the real axes; ac/saves targets land in the buffed DIAGNOSTICS only (the base axes are parity-locked to derive.js).

Divine Favor.note: +1/3 CL luck to attack and damage, max +3.

Divine Power.note: +1/3 CL luck, plus the haste-like extra attack. Does not stack with haste; the scorer takes one extra attack.

Righteous Might.note: Size step (dice up, -1 to hit) plus +4 Str. The Gorum special.

Enlarge Person.note: Dice step and +2 Str; the -2 Dex is folded as the size attack penalty only.

Haste.note: The classic: one extra attack, +1 to hit, +1 dodge AC (AC lands in diagnostics).

Shield of Faith.note: +2 deflection, +1 per 6 CL, max +5 total -- modeled as 2+cl/6 capped. Diagnostics only.

Heroism.note: 10 min/level: up before every fight that matters.

Magic Weapon, Greater.note: Plain-summed over the weapon's own enhancement, per the metric's declared no-typed-stacking doctrine (TYPED_STACKING_NOTE).

Stoneskin.note: DR 10/adamantine while it lasts (10 min/level; the 150gp component is ignored, upper bound). The dr fold takes the max of class DR, text DR and buff DR.

Barkskin.note: +2 +1/3 CL natural armor, max +5. Diagnostics only.

dr._why: The curated class-DR table (dr axis, ruling 2026-08-11). DR never arrives through the change ledger -- the pf1 target vocabulary in this stack has no dr/eres key -- so the axis is this table plus a text harvest over the held buckets whose prose states the CURRENT value (professions, feats, traits). class_ability_desc is not harvested (no level filter -- an L16 fighter carries the 19th-level armor mastery text) and neither are chosen class options (their prose states scaling maxima and conditionals; the first baseline read DR 15 off a level-5 character that way -- choice-granted DR gets curated here instead, per source). DR does not stack; the axis is the max.

fighter_armor_mastery.note: DR 5/- at 19th while armored -- the metric's declared round has the fighter in its armor.

_blind._why: Printed on every profile and in the baseline report. A metric that silently rates a warder at zero is worse than one that says it cannot see maneuvers yet.
offense: spell buffs OUTSIDE the curated spell_buffs table (the table is the sweaty core; curate more rows rather than widening the parser)
favoured enemy and studied target (target-typed bonuses)
kinetic blast (kineticist damage scores weapon-only until a blast rule is authored)
PoW boosts and counters (stance and strike bonus DICE now parse from prose; non-dice riders and the ~12 unparseable maneuvers stay blind)
Spheres talents without structured `changes` (talent prose is not parsed; the base destructive blast has its own rule)
psionic power effects (psionics scores on the caster axis only)
spell damage (casters score on DC and highest-spell-level, not on blast output -- so a Vancian blaster's burst_raw is its weapon, knowingly)
defense: the house-waived ambient Dodge (+1 AC for every Dex 13+ character; folding it would break derive.js parity, which asserts the AC delta is exactly the enhancement shortfall)
DR from sources the dr table does not curate (class DR beyond barbarian/fighter, chosen class options, archetypes, special materials)
energy resistance as an axis (harvested text values ride in diagnostics only)
utility: everything except skill breadth -- no benchmark column exists for utility
